'''Sergei Vladimirovich Bulanov''', ({{langx|ru|Сергей Владимирович Буланов|translit=Sergei Bulanov}}; born August 16, 1947) is a Russian [[physicist]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Персоналии: Буланов Сергей Владимирович|url=http://www.mathnet.ru/rus/person51500|access-date=2020-06-13|website=www.mathnet.ru|language=ru}}</ref> He received the 1983 [[State Prize of the USSR]],  the 2016 [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] (with [[Hartmut Zohm]]) for "''contributions to the development of large-scale next-step devices in high-temperature plasma physics research''",<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mantica|first1=Paola|last2=Dendy|first2=Richard|last3=Jacquemot|first3=Sylvie|date=2016-11-25|title=43rd European Physical Society Conference on Plasma Physics|journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion|language=en|volume=59|issue=1|article-number=010101|doi=10.1088/0741-3335/59/1/010101|issn=0741-3335|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Alfvén Prize {{!}} European Physical Society – Plasma Physics Division|url=http://plasma.ciemat.es/eps/awards/alfven-prize/|access-date=2020-06-13|language=en-US}}</ref> and the [[Order of the Rising Sun|Order of Rising Sun with Gold Rays and Rosette]] in 2020.

== Life and career ==
Bulanov studied [[theoretical astrophysics|theoretical physics]]  and astrophysics at the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] in the 1960s. He was a student of {{ill|Sergei Ivanovich Syrovatskii|ru|Сергей Иванович Сыроватский}} and [[Vitaly Ginzburg]].

He is a Distinguished Research Fellow at the [[National Institutes for Quantum and Radiological Science|National Institute for Quantum and Radiological Science and Technology]] in [[Kyoto, Japan]] and a Head of the Department at the ELI-Beamlines, Dolni Brezany in Czech Republic.

== Scientific contributions ==
Bulanov proposed the idea of [[Theory of relativity|relativistic]] mirrors for generating [[X-ray]]s, whereby a laser beam is reflected by plasma waves and is split up by [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear interactions]] to form a thin layer of relativistic electrons.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bulanov|first1=Sergei V|last2=Esirkepov|first2=Timur Zh|last3=Kando|first3=Masaki|last4=Pirozhkov|first4=Alexander S|last5=Rosanov|first5=Nikolai N|date=2013|title=Relativistic mirrors in plasmas. Novel results and perspectives|journal=Physics-Uspekhi|volume=56|issue=5|pages=429–464|doi=10.3367/ufne.0183.201305a.0449|bibcode=2013PhyU...56..429B|s2cid=121702558 |issn=1063-7869}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bulanov|first1=Sergei V.|last2=Esirkepov|first2=Timur Zh|last3=Kando|first3=Masaki|last4=Koga|first4=James K.|s2cid=119300803|date=2016|title=Relativistic Mirrors in Laser Plasmas (Analytical Methods)|journal=Plasma Sources Science and Technology|volume=25|issue=5|article-number=053001|doi=10.1088/0963-0252/25/5/053001|arxiv=1603.07507|bibcode=2016PSST...25e3001B|issn=1361-6595}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bulanov|first1=Sergei V.|last2=Esirkepov|first2=Timur|last3=Tajima|first3=Toshiki|date=2003|title=Light Intensification towards the Schwinger Limit|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=91|issue=8|article-number=085001|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.91.085001|pmid=14525245|bibcode=2003PhRvL..91h5001B |issn=0031-9007}}</ref> They were intended to be an alternative to [[synchrotron radiation]] sources and [[Free-electron laser|free electron lasers]], and were used in the development of compact radiation sources and for basic research in [[quantum electrodynamics]] (e.g. electron-positron [[pair production]] in vacuum). Bulanov has also worked on [[particle acceleration]] using [[Laser Plasma Acceleration|laser plasmas]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bulanov|first1=Stepan S.|last2=Esirkepov|first2=Timur Zh.|last3=Thomas|first3=Alexander G. R.|last4=Koga|first4=James K.|last5=Bulanov|first5=Sergei V.|s2cid=36857911|date=2010|title=Schwinger Limit Attainability with Extreme Power Lasers|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=105|issue=22|article-number=220407|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.105.220407|pmid=21231373|arxiv=1007.4306|bibcode=2010PhRvL.105v0407B|issn=0031-9007}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Esirkepov|first1=T.Zh.|last2=Bulanov|first2=S.V.|s2cid=118413997|date=2012|title=Fundamental physics and relativistic laboratory astrophysics with extreme power lasers|journal=EAS Publications Series|volume=58|pages=7–22|doi=10.1051/eas/1258001|arxiv=1202.4552|bibcode=2012EAS....58....7E|issn=1633-4760}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Esirkepov|first1=T. Zh.|last2=Bulanov|first2=S. V.|last3=Nishihara|first3=K.|last4=Tajima|first4=T.|last5=Pegoraro|first5=F.|last6=Khoroshkov|first6=V. S.|last7=Mima|first7=K.|last8=Daido|first8=H.|last9=Kato|first9=Y.|last10=Kitagawa|first10=Y.|last11=Nagai|first11=K.|s2cid=32168818|date=2002|title=Proposed Double-Layer Target for the Generation of High-Quality Laser-Accelerated Ion Beams|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=89|issue=17|article-number=175003|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.89.175003|pmid=12398678|bibcode=2002PhRvL..89q5003E|issn=0031-9007}}</ref> and he is a co-author of an idea that proposed using the laser accelerated ions for [[cancer therapy]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bulanov|first1=Sergei V.|last2=Khoroshkov|first2=Vladimir S.|date=2002|title=Feasibility of using laser ion accelerators in proton therapy.|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1134%2F1.1478534|journal=Plasma Phys.
